Sample text:
---
I'll write about the particular quiet of a library at closing time.

The lights don't all go out at once. They dim in sections, like a slow exhale, and the last librarian moves through the stacks with a cart of returned books, her shoes making that soft *shh* sound on the carpet that somehow feels louder than it is. The computers shut down one by one, their screens going black with a little sigh of air from the vents.

There's a specific loneliness to it, but not a sad one. The books have been read, or at least opened, touched, considered. They've done their work for the day. The building settles. The heating clicks on somewhere in the walls. Outside, the parking lot empties of the last few cars, headlights sweeping across the darkened windows.

I think about all the people who were here. The student who fell asleep in the armchair by the window, mouth open, drooling slightly on a calculus textbook. The old man who comes every Tuesday to read the newspaper and never checks anything out. The couple who met in the poetry section in 2019 and still come back to that same aisle, though they're married now, though they don't need to be.

The library doesn't remember them specifically. But it holds the shape of their presence. The worn spot on the carpet. The book left slightly askew. The coffee ring on the table in the café that nobody wiped.

Tomorrow it will fill again. The fluorescent lights will buzz back to life. The doors will slide open and the day will begin its ordinary, necessary work of letting people find what they need.

But for this hour, between closing and locking, the building belongs to itself. To the books. To whatever small gods watch over places that ask nothing of people except that they come, and read, and maybe—maybe—find something that changes them.

I like to think the books notice. I like to think they wait, patient as only paper and glue and thread can be, for the next hand to reach for them.

The last light goes out. The dark is complete. Somewhere, a book settles on its shelf with a sound too small to hear.

Goodnight, library. Goodnight, stories. Goodnight, whoever you are, whoever you were, whoever you will become.
---
